experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: 2.3 Typical Procedure for Pd(OAc)2-Catalyzed C-H Trifluoromethylation. In a 20 mL sealed tube, N-aryl benzamide 1a (33.7 mg, 0.10 mmol, 1.0 equiv.), 5-(trifluoromethyl)dibenzothiophenium trifluoromethanesulfonate 2a (60.3 mg, 0.15 mmol, 1.5 equiv), Pd(OAc)2 (2.3 mg, 0.01 mmol, 10 mol %), Cu(OAc)2 (36.4 mg, 0.20 mmol, 2.0 equiv), N-methylformamide L4 (87.6 uL, 1.5 mmol, 15 equiv), and trifluoroacetic acid (74.3 uL, 1.0 mmol, 10 equiv) were dissolved in 1,2-dichloroethane (3 mL) under N2 atmosphere. The reaction mixture was then tightly capped and stirred for 10 minutes at room temperature for proper mixing of the reactants, and then heated at 130 °C with vigorous stirring for 24 hours. The reaction mixture was then cooled to room temperature, diluted with acetone and filtered through a small pad of Celite. The filtrate was concentrated in vacuo and purified by a silica gel packed flash chromatography column, using acetone/ethyl acetate/hexane (1:1:10) as the eluent. 5-Methyl-N-(2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)-2-(trifluoromethyl)benzamide (3c), yield 94%. 1H NMR (400 MHz, acetone-d6) δ 10.05 (s, 1H), 7.75 (d, J = 8.0 Hz, 1H), 7.62 (s, 1H), 7.58 (d, J = 8.0 Hz, 1H), 2.49 (s, 3H); 19F NMR (375 MHz, acetone-d6) δ -56.04 (t, J = 21.4 Hz, 3F), -58.42 (s, 3F), -143.06 to -143.15 (m, 2F), -143.32 to -143.37 (m, 2F); 13C NMR (100 MHz, acetone-d6) δ 165.67, 143.58, 134.54, 131.62, 129.65, 127.00 (q, J = 4.8 Hz), 124.97 (q, J = 32.0 Hz), 124.28 (q, J = 271.0 Hz), 20.61; HRMS (ESI-TOF) m/z Calcd for C16H8F10NO (M+H)+: 420.0441, found: 420.0443.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: The General Procedure for the Trifluoromethylation Reaction In an oven-dried Schlenk tube, to the solution of free anilines (0.2 mmol) and Togni reagent 3 (1.3-1.6 equiv) in DMF (1.0 mL), was added Ir(ppy)3 (1.5 mol%). Then, the tube was degassed and filled with nitrogen for three times. The resulting reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature by irradiation with blue LEDs (7 W, λmax= 455 nm) for 15-36 hours. When the reaction was finished, saturated NaHCO3 solution (5 mL) was added into the reaction mixture, and extracted with ethyl acetate for four times. The combined organic layers was dried over anhydrous Na2SO4, and concentrated in vacuo. The residue was purified by silica gel chromatography or preparative TLC on GF 254. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the trifluoromethylation of arenes and heteroarenes: A dried Young-type NMR tube was charged with 1-(Trifluoromethyl)-1,2-benziodoxol-3(1H)-one (1, 12.6 mg, 0,04 mmol), 100 μL of a stock solution of perfluoronaphthalene in CDCl3 containing 0.01 mmol (used as internal standard) and 100 μL of a freshly prepared stock solution of methyltrioxorhenium (MTO) in CDCl3 containing 0.08 equivalents (0.003 mmol). To the colourless solution 1.5 equivalents (0,06 mmol) of the aromatic substrate were added and CDCl3 was added to afford a final volume of 0.5 mL. authors: Xie, Jin; Yuan, Xiangai; Abdukader, Ablimit; Zhu, Chengjian; Ma, Jing
reference: Visible-Light-Promoted Radical C-H Trifluoromethylation of Free Anilines | Xie, Jin; Yuan, Xiangai; Abdukader, Ablimit; Zhu, Chengjian; Ma, Jing | Organic Letters (2014), 16(6), 1768-1771
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: The General Procedure for the Trifluoromethylation Reaction In an oven-dried Schlenk tube, to the solution of free anilines (0.2 mmol) and Togni reagent 3 (1.3-1.6 equiv) in DMF (1.0 mL), was added Ir(ppy)3 (1.5 mol%). Then, the tube was degassed and filled with nitrogen for three times. The resulting reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature by irradiation with blue LEDs (7 W, λmax= 455 nm) for 15-36 hours. When the reaction was finished, saturated NaHCO3 solution (5 mL) was added into the reaction mixture, and extracted with ethyl acetate for four times. The combined organic layers was dried over anhydrous Na2SO4, and concentrated in vacuo. The residue was purified by silica gel chromatography or preparative TLC on GF 254. The desired trifluoromethylated anilines. 4-(methylsulfonyl)-2-(trifluoromethyl)aniline 32: 0.2 mmol; 1.6 equiv Togni reagent was used; 76% yield, white solid; m.p. 135-137 °C. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3): δ (ppm) = 7.98 (d, J = 2.0 Hz, 1 H), 7.79 (dd, J = 8.8, 2.0 Hz, 1 H), 6.85 (d, J = 8.8 Hz, 1 H), 4.69 (s, 2 H), 3.05 (s, 3 H); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3): δ (ppm) = 149.1, 132.0, 128.0, 127.4 (q, J = 5.6 Hz), 123.9 (q, J = 271.0 Hz), 117.0, 112.8 (q, J = 30.9 Hz), 44.9; 19F NMR (376 MHz, CDCl3): δ (ppm) = -63.5; HRMS (ESI) m/z calcd for C8H7F3NO2S [M-H]-: 238.0155; found:238.0165.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Acid-Mediated Cyclization of Hemiaminal 2. Hemiaminal 2 (0.17 mmol) was dissolved in 1 mL of solvent (see Table 1 and the Supporting Information); then the acid was added (equivalents as specified in Table 1 and the Supporting Information) under a N2 atmosphere. The reaction tube was sealed with a stopper and stirred at the temperature mentioned in Table 1 and the Supporting Information. After completion, the reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature, quenched with aqueous NaHCO3, and extracted with CH2Cl2 (3 × 2 mL). experimental_procedure: 2.3 Typical Procedure for Pd(OAc)2-Catalyzed C-H Trifluoromethylation. In a 20 mL sealed tube, N-aryl benzamide 1a (33.7 mg, 0.10 mmol, 1.0 equiv.), 5-(trifluoromethyl)dibenzothiophenium trifluoromethanesulfonate 2a (60.3 mg, 0.15 mmol, 1.5 equiv), Pd(OAc)2 (2.3 mg, 0.01 mmol, 10 mol %), Cu(OAc)2 (36.4 mg, 0.20 mmol, 2.0 equiv), N-methylformamide L4 (87.6 uL, 1.5 mmol, 15 equiv), and trifluoroacetic acid (74.3 uL, 1.0 mmol, 10 equiv) were dissolved in 1,2-dichloroethane (3 mL) under N2 atmosphere.
